ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in building decoration, a worker uses a grindstone of mass m to polish an inclined wall. When a vertical upward pushing force of magnitude F is applied to the grindstone, the grindstone just moves upward along the inclined wall with uniform motion. It is known that the coefficient of kinetic friction between the grindstone and the inclined wall is μ, so what is the expression for the magnitude of the friction force received by the grindstone?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there is a grindstone attached to an inclined wall, and the angle θ is marked between the inclined wall and the vertical direction; at the grindstone there is a vertical upward arrow, labeled as the external force F, indicating that a vertical upward pushing force is applied to the grindstone. The grindstone moves upward along the inclined wall. Then reason: The problem statement says that the grindstone moves upward along the inclined wall with uniform motion, so the resultant force along the direction of the inclined wall is zero. Because the angle between the inclined wall and the vertical direction is θ, the component of the vertical upward pushing force F upward along the inclined wall is Fcosθ; gravity mg is vertically downward, and its component along the direction of the inclined wall is mgcosθ, directed downward along the inclined wall. The grindstone moves upward relative to the inclined wall, so the direction of the kinetic friction force is downward along the inclined wall. Write the equilibrium equation along the direction of the inclined wall: Fcosθ - mgcosθ - f = 0. Solving gives the magnitude of the friction force f = (F - mg)cosθ.
